newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada April retail sales rise 1.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada April retail sales rise 1.1 pct.

text.p: Canadian retail sales rose 1.1 percent in April to a seasonally adjusted C$19.12 billion from a revised C$18.91 billion (C$18.88 billion) in March, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
Sales, ex vehicles, s/a +0.7 +6.2 C$14.40 bln

Statistics Canada said early indications for May sales showed a 0.5 decrease in the number of employees in retail trade but a total employment increase of 0.4 percent in May. The number of housing starts in May rose by 4.6 percent from the same period in 1996.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.1 percent rise in retail sales in April after March's 0.8 percent drop.
Statistics Canada said the biggest monthly increase in retail sales in April was in the automotive sector, up 2.0 percent or C$141 million.

StatsCan said advances were also recorded in most of the other retail sectors, with stores classified as other retail rising 3.5 percent, drug stores rising 1.3 percent, clothing stores up 0.8 percent, general merchandise stores up 0.3 percent and furniture stores up 0.5 percent.
Only food stores recorded a decline in sales in April, falling 0.7 percent, the agency said.
Retail sales fell in Manitoba by 4.3 percent in April, StatsCan said. Several other provinces showed declines in April retail sales but none of the magnitude of Manitoba.
Excluding Manitoba, retail sales grew by 1.3 percent in April, the agency said.

In the first quarter of 1997, retail sales have advanced steadily in the past seven months, relecting lower interest rates, StatsCan said. Savings rates declined to 1.7 percent in the first quarter of 1997, the lowest rate of household savings since 1947, the date for which savings rates were first calculated.
Consumer credit rose to C$132.6 billion in March 1997, which is 5.3 percent greater than September 1996, but growth in disposable income has remained modest, the agency said.
